view_Home.txt-2: CAA believes that anarchism is not only a social ideal but also an intellectual tradition that needs to be continuously developed through theoretical study, collective organization, and social practice.
view_Home.txt-10: We hope to promote the development of anarchist thought through sustained research, exchange, and practice.
view_Home.txt-12: Particularism emphasizes building anarchist organizations with a clear theoretical foundation and practical goals, allowing anarchists to participate in social practice more consistently and effectively through collective discussion, organizational development, and social connections.
view_Home.txt-13: CAA pays attention to the realities of Chinese society while also absorbing the historical experiences and theoretical achievements of the international anarchist movement.
view_Home.txt-21: Anarchism's main idea is to oppose all forms of forced, hierarchical authority, especially the state, government, and capitalist system. It suggests that society should be organized through voluntary cooperation, free association, and mutual self-management.
view_Home.txt-23: Oppose all coercive power institutions like the state, church, and military
view_Home.txt-25: All social organizations should be based on free consent, not coercion.
view_Home.txt-27: Oppose the concentration of power, and support local autonomy and federal-style connections
view_Home.txt-29: Believing that cooperation rather than competition is the natural tendency of human society
